candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a well-defined T1-hypointense, STIR-hyperintense lesion with a thick sclerotic rim in the anterolateral cortex of the left femoral head — the classic nidus-with-sclerosis appearance of osteoid osteoma. Night pain, young male, cortical location, and failure of anti-tubercular therapy are all consistent with osteoid osteoma. CRMO is a multifocal autoinflammatory periosteal/metaphyseal condition typically seen in children/adolescents, usually without a discrete cortical nidus with sclerotic rim, and the biopsy showing lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates without granulomas or specific CRMO histology does not support CRMO over osteoid osteoma. The two diagnoses are related (both benign bone lesions causing pain and edema) but represent incompatible subtypes.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: CRMO is a distinct inflammatory bone condition, not osteoid osteoma; both can cause bone pain and marrow edema but differ in etiology, histology, imaging characteristics, and management

case_quality_flags: Classic osteoid osteoma presentation with nidus and sclerotic rim on MRI; CRMO is an incompatible alternative diagnosis rather than a parent or component of osteoid osteoma
